Subject: Recap & procurement path confirmation — FinCo Analytics

Hi Amanda / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our discovery and a few asks to keep procurement moving. High-level takeaways from the call:

- Use case: customer-facing analytics assistant for FinCo Insights (high QPS during market open).
- Data controls: must remain within our VPC; logging retention limited to 90 days.
- SLO priorities: 99th percentile latency under 200ms for short text generation.

Hosting/pricing options we discussed (brief):
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to ship, card and PO supported, on-demand billing; good for pilot/PLG.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool, commit-based pricing available (1/6/12 month tiers), better unit economics for steady QPS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workflows; longer lead time and standard enterprise license.

Attached: SOW-draft-FinCo.pdf (starter SOW) and pricing-grid-FinCo.csv (illustrative rates for hosted/dedicated/private).

Action items / questions for procurement before we loop legal/ops:
1) Preferred procurement route: PO (Net 30/45) v. company card v. marketplace listing?
2) If PO, who is the billing entity and billing contact?
3) Is a vendor marketplace listing required (e.g., AWS Marketplace) to proceed?
4) Any internal paperwork (vendor setup form) we should complete now?

If you can reply with the procurement route and approximate timeline (procurement SLA), I’ll have our billing ops and legal preload the right docs to speed processing.

Proposed next step: 30-min procurement alignment call this week or early next to confirm path and sign off on billing entity. I’ve cc’d Neha from our billing ops to help with PO templates and Aditya from legal will be looped once the preferred path is confirmed.

Thanks,

Amanda — great, appreciate the fast responses and the procurement form. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) Dedicated commits: we support 1-, 6-, and 12-month committed tiers. Discounts are structured as a function of committed spend + expected utilization; there is also a small sustained-usage tier you can enable for excess usage beyond commit. I’ve summarized typical tradeoffs below:

- 1-month commit: modest discount (~10%), fastest to provision for steady pilots.
- 6-month commit: meaningful discount (~20%) and preferred for predictable mid-stage production.
- 12-month commit: best unit economics (~30%+), requires PO/contract upfront.

2) Private/VPC lead times: typical delivery window is 8–12 weeks from PO + signed SOW (this includes network onboarding, KMS setup, and any partner coordination). Dedicated provisioning: 3–6 weeks from PO for standard configs; accelerated provisioning available for an onboarding fee.

To keep procurement moving, proposed checklist for this week:
- FinCo: confirm billing entity + billing contact (Amanda/Jason).
- FinCo: return vendor form (attached) with any required insurance info.
- Redwood: send PO template + estimated lead times for Dedicated/Private (Neha is cc’d and will send templates).
- Redwood: prep two pricing options in HubSpot — (A) Hosted on-demand + short pilot PO, (B) 6-month Dedicated commit with discount and SOW.

I’ve attached an updated pricing-grid that maps hosted vs dedicated vs private with example monthly spends at different QPS bands. If it helps, we can provide a short TCO sketch for 6/12 month commits vs hosted on-demand.

Suggested next step: 30-minute procurement alignment tomorrow (Thu) at 10am PT if that works for you — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm. If procurement prefers Friday, we can do 9am PT.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/fin-2027-089) and a starter DocuSign envelope for the SOW (https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-finco).

Thanks — cc’ing Neha to action PO template and Aditya to flag any legal items in the SOW.
